hook: A very short, quiet file about a sealed shaft on Hashima Island that leads down to a huge underground structure. It is worth reading slowly and checking the footnote, because the whole effect rests on one architectural idea and one closing line.
whyItMatters: 3220 shows how much a minimalist entry can carry with no events at all: no incidents, no interviews, only a description of a building and what sits inside it. A small placard on the hatch reads "Department of Abnormalities" in Japanese, and the article leaves that name entirely unexplained. The procedures amount to pouring concrete into the shaft and forbidding any further exploration, which says more than a warning would.
thingsToNotice: The structure is a panopticon, with two hundred floors of open cells ringed around a central tower of one-way glass that nobody has found a way into. Every cell except one holds a painted concrete figure standing over its drain, turned to face the tower and constantly leaking a dark red substance into a grate whose outlet no one knows. The article says nothing about the empty cell, and then the addendum mentions a hatch on the bottom floor that once led up into the tower's viewing room, where a single skeleton with a broken neck lay. The file never links the empty cell to the dead watcher; it simply places them in the same document and stops.
